title: Uniqueness of restriction across a depth-positive boundary
statement: Let $L$ be a locally Noetherian scheme [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions, def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], $U$ an open subscheme, and $N$ a quasi-coherent module [pqf-def-coherent]. Suppose $N(V)$ is finite over $\mathcal O_L(V)$ for every affine open $V$. Suppose for every $y\notin U$ the stalk $N_y$ is finite and has depth at least one [def-weil-pbc-depth]. Then for every open $V$ the restriction map $N(V)\to (j_*(N|_U))(V)$ is injective, where $j:U\hookrightarrow L$.

source.place: Tags 0B3M, 05AR and 00LL; injectivity step of Tag 0E9I

proof.text: Work on a Noetherian affine open V. Its module N(V) is finite. Positive depth at a boundary point gives a nonzerodivisor in the maximal ideal, so that ideal cannot be associated to the stalk. Associated and weakly associated points coincide on locally Noetherian schemes (05AR). Hence all weakly associated points lie in U.

A section vanishing on V intersect U has cyclic image subsheaf supported outside U. Its weakly associated points are among those of N, and also in its support. There are none. A module with no weakly associated points is zero. This is the argument of 0B3M and proves injectivity on V.

For arbitrary V cover V by affine opens. Two sections with the same restriction to V intersect U agree on each affine member by the preceding argument, so separatedness makes them equal. The unit component is restriction by Mathlib restrictAdjunction_unit_app_app.
